title: Compiler Dependency Inventory — Karkain 1.1.0 (Stable)

revision_notes.what_changed: The `native` component did not exist in the phase-144 revision: the C-free native backend (increment 150) and its self-hosted ownership (increment 151) were both later. The KIR statement was corrected: the revision said 'KIR text does not yet feed the backend' and that the ownership target was 'KIR-consumption and kcc-native test-driver assembly (Phase 145+)'. The first half is still true and is now stated as a LIMITATION; the second half is obsolete because the kcc-native path ships.
revision_notes.what_did_not_change: The frontend, the semantic analysis, the assembly ownership and the bootstrap contract are unchanged since phase 144. The bootstrap is still Go-primary plus gcc, and the self-hosting proof (increment 154) is still carried out of v1.2.0 to v1.3.0 as UNMET.

scope: The single source of truth for what the Karkain compiler holds today, what it owns on the path to self-hosting, and which Go/C components are bootstrap infrastructure versus compiler responsibility. Phases 121 (Compiler Independence Foundation) and 122 (Compiler Pipeline Ownership) treat this inventory as their baseline.

lexer.active_path: kcc (self-hosted) is the default engine for check/build/run; its lexer is src/compiler/lexer.kark. Go lexer serves LSP, fmt, the bootstrap stage-1 (KARKAIN_ENGINE=go), and Go-front-end fallbacks.

parser.go: pkg/parser (13 files), entry parser.go, phase120 makes print(value) and print value parity
parser.active_path: kcc parses with src/compiler/parser.kark; bootstrap stage-1 and Go tooling parse with pkg/parser.

ast.active_path: kcc builds src/compiler ASTs; Go builds pkg/parser ASTs.

semantic_analysis.active_path: kcc check/build/run run the self-hosted checker for compiler-internal passes; the Go resolver powers runSemanticPreflight/kccTargetPreflight which gate BOTH engines at the CLI layer (K002/K102 errors, exit 3).

kir.go: NONE (Go only routes: pkg/cli/kir.go KCCKirCommand + KCCKirVerifyCommand)
kir.active_path: kcc kir / karkain kir emit deterministic KIR v1 text via src/compiler/kir.kark. Phase 121 makes KIR an engine-internal invariant: kirVerify runs inside checkFile on the default kcc check path (silent on success, error[K121] + exit 3 on drift) and standalone via kcc verifykir / karkain kir --verify. KIR text does not yet feed ANY backend, and that is a LIMITATION rather than a leftover: the native driver (native_value.kark) consumes the PARSED AST directly, not the KIR text. KIR is verified on the default check path as an engine invariant, and it is emitted on demand; making it the backend input is not done.

assembly.karkain: src/compiler/main.kark assembleProject + helpers (moduleImportNames, stripModuleImports, siblingContent, moduleDirSource, resolveStdlibModule, resolveUserModule, marker-gated findStdlibRoot)
assembly.active_path: Phase 122: kcc composes its OWN input for FLAT projects (no karkain.toml; imports std.* or sibling-resolvable) on the real CLI path â€” check/build/run/kir/verifykir all stage through kccStageInput (sandbox mirror + lib/ stdlib tree) and assemble in assembleProject. The compiler's own 10-file tree, examples/module_system and examples/stdlib_v2 all assemble this way. Manifest / workspace / package-manager assemblies and transitive non-local resolution keep the Go module-aware kccAssembleSource/resolveSourcesRun (documented BRIDGE).

codegen.go: pkg/codegen (63 files), entry codegen.go (C23 emit + native/DWARF/SIMD/WASM/npu)
codegen.active_path: kcc build/run use src/compiler/codegen.kark; bootstrap stage-1 uses pkg/codegen.

native.karkain: src/compiler/native_emit.kark (the x86-64 encoder), native_value.kark (the whole-program driver), native_elf.kark / native_pe.kark / native_macho.kark (the three container writers)
native.go: pkg/native is a REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION only: program.go (the driver), emit.go (the encoder), elf.go / pe.go / macho.go (the containers)
native.active_path: kcc owns ALL THREE C-free native targets (native-x86_64-windows, native-x86_64-linux, native-x86_64-macos). The seam is pkg/cli/kcc_native.go: kccNativeOwnedTargets names the targets, kccNativeValidateImage runs the ORACLE's container validator over kcc's bytes, and there is deliberately NO call into the Go writer -- an image that could not be attributed to kcc is the dishonesty this seam exists to remove.
native.status: ACTIVE (kcc). pkg/native is a reference: it supplies the byte-identity differential, the container validators (Parse / ParsePE / ParseMachO) and the reference implementation the gates compare against. It is NOT on the compilation path for a native target.

runtime.go: pkg/codegen preamble helpers (C strings), pkg/runtime gate harnesses
runtime.active_path: Generated C links against the embedded runtime helpers emitted by both codegen paths.

bootstrap.contract: stage-1: Go front end emits src/compiler/main.c; gcc links kcc.exe. Bootstrap identity gate asserts stage2 == stage3 bitwise.
bootstrap.active_path: kccBinaryPath rebuilds kcc.exe when any src/compiler/*.kark is newer (kccStale).

pipeline.source: desc('assembly -> lexer -> parser -> AST -> semantic analysis -> KIR -> code generation -> runtime -> executable')
pipeline.kir_invariant: KIR is verified by the compiler itself on the default kcc check path (kirVerify in checkFile, error[K121] on drift). Text remains on-demand (kcc kir / karkain kir); wiring it into build/run as the codegen input is a post-121 boundary.
pipeline.flat_assembly_ownership: since Phase 122 the compiler composes its own input for flat projects (assembleProject in src/compiler/main.kark); Go only stages it into a sandbox (kccStageInput + lib/ mirror). Non-flat (manifest/workspace/PM) assemblies remain Go-owned.
pipeline.manifest_assembly_ownership: Karkain-owned since Phase 144: manifestDepRecords/lockLookup/depSourceDir/projectDepSources in src/compiler/main.kark; Go stages (kccMirrorProject) but never injects.

ownership_horizon.current: kcc assembles manifest/workspace/registry dependencies itself (projectDepSources, Phase 144) on top of the Phase 122 flat assembly; the CLI mirrors project trees for kcc-native assembly and injects nothing.
ownership_horizon.ultimate: KCC self-hosting: the Karkain compiler rebuilds itself with no Go compiler front-end responsibility.

invariants: path-less `source: <basename>` header and `[ok] kir text: N lines` marker
byte-deterministic output for identical input across runs and sandboxes
parse errors surface before emission (exit 3), never a partial `[ok]`
structural_rules: header line exactly `KIR v1`; source line names exactly the basename
two-space indentation per depth level; nesting depth never jumps forward by more than one level
every statement line ends ` line: <decimal>` except `block` and `stmt <type>`
verified by kirVerify inside checkFile on the default kcc check path (error[K121] + exit 3 on drift)
kir_contract.serialization: text v1, one line per statement, depth-indented, all expression forms parenthesized

tools_contract_144.lsp: Go-only, frozen boundary (no kcc LSP surface exists).
tools_contract_144.pm_commands: Go CLI surface (add/fetch/update/publish operate on manifests/locks); resolution-for-assembly is kcc-native since 144A.
tools_contract_144.incremental: Go build path only (pkg/compiler); kcc has no cache.
tools_contract_144.wasm_wit: Go backends (explicit post-108 boundary, unchanged by 144).
tools_contract_144.test_runner: kcc owns discovery/drivers (Phase 96); Go injects module scope for manifest projects (kccTestSource) — test-driver migration is the documented next slice.
